How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, February 6, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Ding
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. BLACK HISTORY MONTH

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of January 16, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of January 16, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. EXCHANGE OF PROPOSITION A FUNDS IN THE AMOUNT OF $500,000

  The City of San Gabriel receives over $1.1 million annually in Proposition (Prop)
  A Local Return Funds from Los Angeles County to be used for the benefit of
  public transit. Approximately $682,000 of the funds are used to operate the
  City’s Dial-A-Ride and Recreation transit programs each year. Since the City
  does not have any other eligible projects and must use these funds within a
  three-year period, it has now accumulated a balance of about $626,000 as of
  June 30, 2023, in unspent Prop A funds. Los Angeles County Metro allows
  agencies to exchange Prop A funds for unrestricted general fund revenue at a
  discounted rate – a practice that San Gabriel has taken advantage of in the past.
  Foothill transit has offered to exchange $500,000 of the City’s Prop A Funds for
  $375,000 in unrestricted funds, representing a rate of $.75/$1.00.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the agreement with the Foothill Transit Authority
  authorizing the exchange of $500,000 in Proposition A Funds for $375,000 in
  general fund revenue.

  D. PURCHASE OF A NEW GRACO BRAND CONCRETE GRINDER WITH A
  LAZERVAC SYSTEM AND CYCLONE FILTER FOR THE FIELD OPERATIONS
  DIVISION FOR A TOTAL COST OF $16,319.21

  The Public Works Department is responsible for maintaining the safety of
  sidewalks and walkways throughout the City. Public Works strives to efficiently
  repair and replace damaged sidewalks, curbs, and gutters throughout the City
  in a timely manner to improve walkability and mitigate trip hazards. This item
  requests Council’s approval for the purchase of a new Graco brand Concrete
  Grinder with a LazerVac System and Cyclone Filter (Grinder) for repairs and
  maintenance to damaged concrete sidewalks throughout the City. The adopted
  fiscal year 2023-24 budget includes $15,000 in the Special Gas Tax Project
  Account No. 124-800-41-99-765. Staff is requesting that the balance of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  3
   $1,319.21 is charged to the Field Operations Special Departmental Account No.
  121-800-02-21-000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  a purchase order with NAC Supply in the amount of $16,319.21 from the Special
  Gas Tax Project Account No. 124-800-41-99-765 and Field Operations Special
  Departmental Account No. 121-800-02-21-000.

  E. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH RKA CONSULTING GROUP
  AND VCA CODE GROUP FOR BUILDING AND SAFETY AND CODE
  ENFORCEMENT SERVICES

  In September of 2023, City staff issued a Request for Proposal to qualified firms
  for Building and Safety and Code Enforcement services within the Community
  Development Department. The significant number of current development
  projects as well as increasing community needs has generated a demand for
  supplemental staff to assist with work overflow. This includes permit issuance,
  building and code enforcement inspections, and plan check review services. The
  agreements with RKA Consulting Group and VCA Code Group will include a
  three-year term with an option to extend the term for an additional year.
  Funding for the services rendered will be from the Community Development
  Department’s budgeted Contractual Services Account Nos. (Building and
  Safety: 121-810-16-22-000 and/or Neighborhood Improvement Services: 121-
  810-19-22-000) in the General Fund at the fixed fee rate.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with RKA Consulting Group and VCA Code Group for Building and
  Safety and Code Enforcement services, and authorize the City Manager or his
  designee to execute the agreements.

  F. INTER-CON SECURITY SYSTEMS INCORPORATED CONTRACT EXTENSION
  FOR PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2024

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  4
   The City initially entered into a three-year service contract with the option to
  extend for an additional two years with Inter-Con Security Systems Inc. In June
  2021, the City elected to execute a two-year extension, with the final contract
  expiring on June 30, 2023. On July 1, 2023, the City entered an additional six-
  month extension which expired on December 31, 2023. Parking enforcement
  services are currently budgeted in the Police Department’s Contractual Services
  Account No.121-751-00-22-000 in the amount of $350,000 for fiscal year 2023-
  24 due to forecasted cost escalations.. The estimated cost for this six-month
  edition is $149,403 ($298,806 / 2).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter a
  six-month contract with Inter-Con ending on June 30, 2024. At that time, Staff
  will re-evaluate their services and/or seek other opportunities for services for
  the remainder of fiscal year 2024.

  G. ADOPTION OF UPDATED “VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED” (VMT)
  THRESHOLDS OF SIGNIFICANCE FOR PURPOSES OF ANALYZING
  TRANSPORTATION IMPACTS UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT (CEQA) [RESOLUTION NO. 24-03]

  In 2020, the City, with guidance provided by the San Gabriel Valley Council of
  Governments (SGVCOG), adopted new CEQA thresholds of significance for
  transportation impacts due to changes in state law. These changes modified
  how the City evaluates projects for transportation impacts for the purposes of
  CEQA. After receiving confirmation from 26 cities to participate in the VMT
  Analysis Model, the SGVCOG confirmed that the total cost per city to participate
  in the study would not exceed $15,000 for the entirety of the five-year (2020-
  2025) contract (including the update phase and maintenance and SGVCOG
  project management costs.) Funding will be included as part of the fiscal year
  2023-24 budget in Account No. 184-800-00-22-000.

  This report describes the changes in VMT, more specifically the change in the
  number of low VMT areas that meet the low VMT screening criterion, discusses
  the SGVCOG recommendations, and includes a draft Resolution to adopt the
  updated CEQA transportation thresholds.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The Resolution has
  been assessed in accordance with the authority and criteria contained in the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  5
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the State CEQA Guidelines, and
  environmental regulations of the City. The adoption of new local CEQA thresholds
  of significance for transportation impacts and the adoption of new Local
  Transportation Assessment Guidelines will not have a significant environmental
  impact and are exempt from the CEQA pursuant to Section 15308 of Title 14 of
  the California Code of Regulations because the two actions are undertaken by
  the City for the protection of the environment. The revised CEQA thresholds will
  be compliant with a Senate mandate (SB 743) and will be used in a regulatory
  process (CEQA process) that involves procedures from the protection of the
  environment. Accordingly, the City Council will consider the recommendation to
  find the Resolution exempt from the environmental review requirements of CEQA
  pursuant to Section 15308 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-03 approving
  the proposed update thresholds of significance and finding that the action is
  exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW THAT WOULD ALLOW MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 ZONE (ZTA23-004)

  The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1186 (“SB 1186”) in 2022, entitled
  the Medicinal Cannabis Patient’s Right of Access Act, which precludes cities and
  counties from adopting or enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect
  of prohibiting the retail sale of medicinal cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 took
  effect on January 1, 2024. The fiscal year 2023-24 Adopted Budget includes the
  cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The City reviewed
  the environmental impacts of the proposed ordinance pursuant to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code Sections 21000, et sq. “CEQA”)
  and the CEQA Guidelines. CEQA guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) provides that a
  project is exempt from CEQA if the activity is covered by the commonsense
  exemption that CEQA only applies to projects which have the potential for
  causing a significant effect on the environment. The proposed ordinance qualifies
  for this CEQA exemption as there is no possibility that the ordinance will have a
  significant effect on the environment as it amends the City’s Municipal Code to
  impose operating requirements on delivery-only medicinal cannabis retailers,

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  6
   which does not effect the environment. Accordingly, the ordinance is not subject
  to further environmental review.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 702.
  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 702 by title only:
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO MEDICINAL CANNABIS
  DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 (LIGHT MANUFACTURING)
  ZONE, SUBJECT TO A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT
  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  OTHER OPTIONS FOR CONSIDERATION

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications, or
  deny the proposed zone text amendment. If the City Council determines that the
  proposed applications or any part of the applications should be denied, the
  appropriate motion should be adopted.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 COMMUNITY BUDGET SURVEY RESULTS, BUDGET
  CALENDAR, AND BUDGET PRIORITIES

  The preparation of the fiscal year 2024-25 budget kicked-off on January 25th as
  department directors were provided budget worksheets to make each
  department’s budget request. Typically, departmental operations exhibit
  consistency from year to year, with incremental adjustments made to ongoing
  activities and allocations for infrequent one-time expenditures. To gain a better
  understanding of community priorities, a community budget survey was
  conducted. Additionally, to align budget priorities with the City Council’s vision,
  this item is brought forth to initiate the discussion of budget priorities for the
  upcoming fiscal year. As the budget process unfolds, there will be multiple
  opportunities to weigh in and refine the fiscal year 2024-25 City budget for
  both the City Council and the public.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  7
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report as well as
  confirm the budget priorities for the fiscal year 2024-25.

  B. BUSINESS LICENSE TAX  STUDY  RESULTS  AND  TAX  CHANGE
  RECOMMENDATIONS

  In August of 2023, the City contracted with HDL Companies to perform a study
  of the City’s business license tax code and to provide recommendations to
  improve the code. The City’s business license code has not been updated for
  decades and includes outdated fee structures and classifications. The HDL
  Companies was tasked with analyzing the City’s business license tax code and
  providing options to the City to help create a fee structure that is fair equitable,
  and keeps pace with inflation.

  The proposed recommendation, model 1 with a 20% increase to flat rates and
  administrative modifications, will generate an estimated additional $329,600 in
  locally derived revenue which will be critical to enhance City services.

  Alternative recommendation no. 1, a 10% increase to flat rates versus a 20%
  increase will generate an additional $251,900 in locally derived revenue.

  Model 2A, a single classification gross receipts tax of $1.25 per $1,000 in gross
  receipts will generate an estimated $730,500 in additional tax revenue.

  Model 2B, a single classification gross receipts tax of $1.50 per $1,000 in gross
  receipts will generate an estimated $985,500 in additional revenue.

  Model 3A, five classification gross receipts tax that ranges from $1.00 to $3.00
  per $1,000 in gross receipts will generate an estimated $1,126,000 in additional
  revenue.

  Model 3B, five classification gross receipts tax that ranges from $1.50 to $3.50
  per $1,000 in gross receipts will generate an estimated $1,635,000 in additional
  revenue.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  8
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to bring back a resolution
  to place Model 1 changes to the business license tax code on the November
  2024 ballot which will enhance the City services and increase fairness within the
  tax code:

  Model 1 Changes
  ► Implement 20% increase to the flat rates.
  ► Add a commercial rental category - assessed at $.75 per $1,000 in gross
  receipts.
  ► Add a catch-all miscellaneous category - assessed at $.50 per $1,000 in gross
  receipts.
  ► For residential rentals:
  o Remove the four units or more requirement. All residential rentals will be
  subject to a tax.
  o Eliminate the $450 cap on the tax.
  ► Cap the penalty for unpaid taxes to 150% of the tax amount.
  ► Add a provision to annually increase the flat rate taxes by the October 2024
  consumer price index.
  ► Replace the coin-operated machines/vending machines with the catch-all
  miscellaneous category.
  ► Remove the $1,050 not-to-exceed provision in the tax code.

  Alternative Recommendation No. 1:
  ► Implement model 1 as noted in the recommendation except implement a 10%
  increase to flat rates instead of a 20% increase.

  Alternative Recommendation No. 2:
  ► Implement a gross receipts single classification model (model 2) or
  multiclassification model (model 3).

  Alternative Recommendation No. 3:
  ► Maintain the current tax code and do not take a tax increase measure to voters
  in November 2024.

  C. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH SUPPORTING ARMS FOR A
  SAN GABRIEL CERTIFIED FARMERS MARKET AND BUDGET
  APPROPRIATION OF $21,000 FOR MARKET LAUNCH AND OPERATION

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 6, 2024  9
   The City Council requested that staff explore the possibility of a potential
  farmers market in San Gabriel. After meeting with the previous farmers market
  operator, evaluating surrounding farmers markets, collecting community
  feedback via an online survey and visiting potential famers market operators,
  staff presents a proposal to launch a weekly farmers market in conjunction with
  Supporting Arms beginning Spring 2024 at the Park & Ride lot in the Mission
  District. A budget of $21,000 should be allocated to cover equipment rental
  costs as well as advertising and marketing efforts for fiscal year 2023-24.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Review and approve the Professional Services Agreement with Supporting
  Arms;
  2. Allocate a $21,000 budget for market operation and marketing efforts;
  3. Approve a modified business license fee structure for a farmers market; and
  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute and sign the agreement.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, February 20, 2023

  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at

  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Finance Director
  William Kaholokula, Community Development Director
  Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus, and Management Assistant

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Assistant City Clerk Bonus provided information for the public on how to view the meeting

   11
  G. ADOPTION OF UPDATED VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED" (VMT) THRESHOLDS

I  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW THAT WOULD ALLOW MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 ZONE (ZTA23-004)

  Mayor Harrington opened the public hearing.

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included that only an M-1 zone would allow this conditional
  use; signage; requiring cameras in the parking lot; and fees.

  Andrew, resident, questioned the difference between medicinal cannabis delivery
  and commercial cannabis delivery, whether pharmacies could sell medicinal
  cannabis, whether the number of cannabis delivery businesses would be limited,
  and where such businesses would be allowed.

I  Mayor Harrington closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included clarification that no manufacturing would take place; cameras
  in the parking lot; limiting the number of businesses; signage; the ordinance would
  apply to delivery of medicinal cannabis only; potential health issues in case of a
  fire; distance between businesses; insurance provisions; and regulating delivery
  destination.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Council Member
  Menchaca, to continue the public hearing to the regular City Council meeting of
  February 20, 2024.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE

  RECOMMENDATIONS

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included statistics on various kinds of businesses; short-term
  rentals are currently not allowed; details of staff report Model choices; public

I  outreach regarding any proposed changes; the potential effect of the City having

  changes to take effect; vacancy rate does not affect tax rate for rental units; taxing
  accessory dwelling units (ADUs); street vendors; embedding Consumer Price Index

  short-term rentals; adjusting equity between types of businesses; adjusting for CPI;
  conducting surveys of residents and business owners; effect of short-term rentals
  on hotel business; and concern about the effect of short-term rentals on neighbors
  and the City and regulation.

I  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to agendize a future
  discussion on short-term rental regulation, and to return with an equitable
  business license tax structure proposal.
